data.description:
## Why
The 1.0 candidate must remain usable while forty agents stream, wait and restart over days; short green tests cannot answer whether memory or typing deteriorates. Backlog item: F2.

## Evidence
- All c11 code citations below are on origin/main `0ff8887e5e`; upstream citations are on upstream/main `920ff39ff7`.
- c11: `Sources/MainThreadHangMonitor.swift:325` owns the watchdog and local hang log, with a 2-second detection threshold documented at `:331` and bounded files at `:373`. `tests_v2/test_socket_reliability_stress.py:105` exercises rapid surface creation, not a 72-hour mixed fleet.
- Research: BACKLOG.md F2/D21/D22; Fable §3 and §7 fleet gate; Astra §3 acceptance example 6; report 05 Top ten items 8 and 9 (GPU and sidebar risks). Upstream #5857/#7050/#10815/#10922 and #8211/#7117/#8270 motivate measurement; they do not authorize ports here.

## Scope
In: reproducible mixed Claude/Codex/Grok fleet workload, 40 agents for 72 hours on Atlas, hang/memory/IOSurface/typing/switching/restart measurements, week-1 baseline, and a 16 GB physical or constrained-host run. Out: sidebar rewrite (D21), automatic GPU reclaim (D22 unless separately admitted from evidence), bug implementations, and release publishing.

## Approach
Build a bounded, restartable harness around tagged artifacts, existing hang telemetry and machine-readable samples. Record source SHA, provider versions, host/display conditions, agent mix, workload and elapsed coverage. Pre-register numeric budgets and pass/fail calculation before measuring any candidate. Use the same workload for baseline and candidate; missing samples, aborted runs and adapter outages remain visible. A constrained-host report must state what was constrained, including any limits that do not emulate physical GPU/shared memory.

## Acceptance criteria
1. In week 1, produce a baseline on the then-current main with exact SHA and versioned workload; record pre-registered latency, hang, memory-growth and IOSurface budgets before a candidate run begins.
2. Execute the final exact candidate with 40 mixed Claude, Codex and Grok agents for 72 hours on Atlas, including attention storms and prescribed restart cycles; retain duration, population and failure evidence instead of calling a shortened run complete.
3. Report hang episodes, memory and IOSurface curves, typing-latency baseline/comparison and tab/workspace switching behavior. The machine-readable gate fails or reports incomplete when a registered budget or coverage requirement is missed.
4. Complete one documented 16 GB Mac or constrained-host run and compare it to the same declared budgets/workload; distinguish simulated constraints from physical hardware evidence.
5. Publish local review artifacts that answer whether sidebar work or GPU reclaim has evidence to justify follow-up. The harness does not silently implement either parked feature.

## Validation
Exercise harness sampling, interruption and result classification with deterministic traces, then run the real tagged mixed fleet and 72-hour candidate soak on Atlas after F1. Capture an actual computer-use typing/switching path on a verified display with a termination timer and dismissal. Keep raw provider content out of public artifacts. A release gate report and Atin’s artifact approval are separate.

## Dependencies
Depends on F1 / C11-216. Baseline must not wait for J2 or the final integrated candidate. Coordinate failure findings with existing hang tickets C11-197/C11-202/C11-205 and PTY tickets C11-130/C11-169/C11-235; do not duplicate them.

## Risks
The harness itself can perturb timing or saturate the host. Sampling must be bounded/off-main, and restarts target only the isolated tagged app. Do not run the fleet on Hyperion. New report/UI labels need localization if product-facing; logs must not disclose private paths, accounts or prompts.

Size: M. Tier: P0. Doctrine check: optional observation and c11-owned storage only; no tenant configuration writes, automatic answers or trust broadening.
data.title: Gate c11 1.0 with a measured 40-agent fleet soak

data.reason:
Soak auth, before any live fleet. Recommend 1.

1. API keys with a $25 cap, passed only as the tagged launch environment. No writes under ~/.claude, ~/.codex, or ~/.grok. Interactive Max, Pro, and SuperHeavy quotas stay available. Needs the keys present on Atlas.
2. Subscription CLIs on the cheapest models. No new keys. About 100 short turns an hour on whichever call-sign is logged in on Atlas, for the 12h baseline and later the 72h candidate.
3. Hold the live fleet. Planning is done either way. Wave 1 does not start until one of these is chosen.

data.body:
Amendment, before any soak has run. The ticket text says 72h. That wording is superseded by the rulings that set an overnight run.

Source:
- Seat brief `.lattice/orchestration/c11-1.0/briefs/soak.md`: baseline on current main in wave 1, overnight candidate in wave 3.
- BACKLOG F2, `upstream-triage/c11-1.0/BACKLOG.md`: "40 mixed agents (Claude, Codex, Grok) for an overnight run on Atlas."
- Orchestrator amendment: candidate pre-registered complete at 10h, with restarts at 30 min, 3h, and 7h. Baseline is 3h with the same workload and probes, because it gates wave 1 to wave 2. Constrained stays 2.5h.

What changed in `soak-budgets-2`:
- Coverage floors are 3h, 10h, and 2.5h. Shorter than the registered duration is incomplete.
- The 3h baseline includes `restart-30m` only. `restart-3h` is the baseline's endpoint, so it is not inside that run. The 10h candidate includes `restart-30m`, `restart-3h`, and `restart-7h`.
- The clean-baseline hang floor is one short watched hang per 10h. Two fail. The old 1/24h floor belonged to the 72h wording.
- Whole-gate cost, including one 10h retry, is about $5.55 under a $10 cap.
- `execute` stops the run above 3× the planned turn rate. The first hour is scored against one hour, so the launch burst does not trip it.
- `--auth api` and `--auth subscription` both run. API keys stay in the process environment and off the command line. Subscription strips those three variables from the launch environment. The choice remains Atin's.

Local commit `339dffea2c` on `c11-1.0/C11-270-fleet-soak`. Not pushed. No soak has started.

Atin 2026-10-01: soak billing = option 2, subscription. Use the subscription CLIs logged in on Atlas on the cheapest models; no API keys. Atin waived usage worry for this run: if a limit is hit, it is handled then.

Atin chose subscription auth. It is the default and the only planned mode for the baseline, the overnight candidate, and the constrained run.

`driver.py run` uses subscription when `--auth` is omitted. No API key is required. The launch drops `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and `XAI_API_KEY` if they were inherited. The `api` branch remains in the driver and is not a planned run.

No soak has started. Local commit `22e4e201bc` on `c11-1.0/C11-270-fleet-soak`. Not pushed.

data.note: Atin chose subscription. It is the default and the only planned mode. No API keys.

data.body: Board convention (Astra plan audit finding 4): C11-259, 260, 261, 262, 294, 295, 302, 303 are related_to this ticket, not depends_on. They are gated on milestone M1 (budgets + 3h baseline incl. g60 control published as a comment on this ticket), not on ticket completion. Completion = M2, the final overnight candidate passed on the integrated artifact.

Astra whole-plan audit, must-fix 4. One ticket, two milestones. M1 is budgets and the 3h baseline published, including a collected g60 control, and it gates wave 1 to wave 2. M2 is the final candidate passed, and it gates release. The ticket is not completed at M1.

The baseline keeps flat-51 and also collects g60: 60 workspaces, g60-v1 tab types and pins, ungrouped on this SHA. The probe counts the expected input glyph or the selected-workspace result in a bounded region, excluding cursor, title, and unrelated output. Each run reserves an Atlas window with no concurrent build or other UI driver.

Plan text only. No soak has started. Local commit `fc7113e41c` on `c11-1.0/C11-270-fleet-soak`. Not pushed.

Codex takeover, planning only. Actor agent:codex-soak; worktree c11-1.0-soak; inherited HEAD fc7113e41cacebf306098f1c5726d81d78e1466d preserved; source citations checked against origin/main 0ff8887e5e965400b01645ef40b85fd0b2605cf2.

Re-stored C11-270 plan after static verification of the inherited harness and Astra audit finding 4. M1 is baseline/budgets/g60 publication; M2 is the exact overnight candidate plus constrained evidence. C11-310 remains folded into the same artifact and has no separately admitted Swift implementation.

Build-mode corrections are specified for the bundled CLI path, complete pretty-printed launch JSON, live TTY/provider population and completion observations, probe-shell focus and expected-result capture, bounded watchdog/partial artifacts, matched g60 phases, artifact provenance/coverage, same-stack sidebar attribution, and real constrained-host admission. Planned versions are soak-budgets-3 / soak-workload-2. Numeric deltas, role durations and subscription auth are unchanged. The inherited scripts remain versions 2/1 and must be aligned before M1; no executable readiness or runtime pass is claimed.

The prior owner's reported unit checks are labeled inherited evidence. This takeover ran no tests, builds or fleet, made no commits or pushes, and did not access or change Atlas. Three local documentation files were amended; the revised plan and protocol attachment carry the durable planning record. No open human decision. Wait for the Orchestrator's BUILD MODE and C11-216's tagged artifact/route before implementation or execution.

Atin ruling (2026-10-01 ~21:35 PDT, via c11 1.0 Orchestrator): the soak is low priority and does not run until all other c11 1.0 work is done.

- M1 no longer gates wave 1 to wave 2, and no consumer (C11-259/260/261/262/294/295/302/303) waits on it. Those tickets prove performance with targeted measurements on their own tagged Atlas builds against a main build.
- At the end, run M1 on a build of the pre-1.0 base (0ff8887e5e or the last pre-1.0 main SHA, recorded) and M2 on the sign-off candidate, back to back on Atlas. The baseline is a build of an old SHA, so running it late loses no comparability.
- Not admitted until the Orchestrator says so. Soak agent mix and the 16 GB host stay open questions for Atin at that point.
